newsitem.title: MACEDONIA: Macedonians protest against pyramid scheme collapse. [CORRECTED 09:30 GMT 11/5]
newsitem.headline: Macedonians protest against pyramid scheme collapse. [CORRECTED 09:30 GMT 11/5]

text.p: Five thousand savers who lost money in the bankruptcy of Macedonia's TAT pyramid investment scheme demonstrated for the return of their money on Saturday in the southern town of Bitola.
According to official data, 23,000 savers lost about 112 million German marks ($66.3 million) in the country's worst financial scandal two months ago.

Tome Nevenovski, leader of the assocation of savers, announced plans last week for a campaign of civil disobedience and warned the government: "If necessary, we will take our money back with weapons".

Demonstrators rejected a government offer to give people with deposits of over 50,000 marks a total of 500 marks a month for the next six months. This would have cost the state about 20 million marks.
The association is demanding guarantees from the state that all deposits will be paid back in full together with the originally offered interest, which varied between three and 10 percent a month.

Ljupco Georgijevski, leader of the biggest opposition party IMRO-DPMNY, called on savers to join an opposition rally in the capital Skopje on May 15 to demand the resignation of the government and early elections.
Georgijevski blamed Prime Minister Branko Crvenkovski and his government for allowing organised crime to flourish in Macedonia.
"In the past we imported criminals -- now we have enough to export," Georgijevski said.
IMRO-DPMNY pastponed its protest from March 27 to give the government time to sort out the TAT financial problem.
"Nothing has been resolved and we will show our dissatisfaction with the political, economic and social situation in in the country," Georgijevski said.
The TAT affair has shaken the economy and weakened the position of Crvenkovski's ruling Social Democratic Alliance.
TAT's owner, Sonja Nikolovska, spent almost two months in police custody but was released after paying one million marks in bail.
Bitola mayor Siljan Micevski, also arrested on suspicion of involvement in the scandal, is out on bail of 700,000 marks.
(Corrects name of pyramid scheme from TAP to TAT).
